newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends easier after lacklustre session.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends easier after lacklustre session.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar eased to a weaker close on Monday after a lacklustre session.
"The focus is clearly elsewhere at the moment with what's been happening in the Aussie, the U.S. dollar and some of the Asian currencies," said a bank chief dealer.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.6909/16 and at 67.53 on its Trade Weighted Index, down from 0.6918/25 and 67.63 at the open.
It traded a narrow 0.6912-21 range on the day and closed on its lows.
Dealers said a 0.5 percent rate cut in Australia last week would have long-term implications for the Kiwi.
"I think the Aussie's going to remain heavy and I think eventually that will impact on the Kiwi," said the chief dealer.
"But we've also been seeing in the last two or three days' trading switching out of Aussie and into Kiwi, and that's been part of the reason why Kiwi's staying quite well supported," he added.
The New Zealand unit was seen trading a 0.6900-30 range overnight.
